text: Let me start by saying that the first Bioshock is one of my all time favorite games. Bioshock 2.. well.. I liked it. Definitely not the first, but definitely awesome. Infinite, while it was a fun play, should not be able to have the name Bioshock in it. It was, first of all, really short. Second of all, it didn't have anything we love about bioshock other than an untrustworthy leader and random vending machines that dispense ammo. In Rapture, those nonsenical things, made a type of sense because the entire place was somehwat nonsensical. The game, in itself, is worth 4 stars. The Bioshock name is why I gave it 3. It is without a doubt worth playing, and it will be fun and interesting. But certain features annoyed me so much when being stoked for another Bioshock installment. For instance, you can only carry 2 guns. None of them are all that cool. In Bioshock 1&2 you can carry like 5 or 6 weapons and in B2 one of them is an awesome drill. The vigors in this game don't actually make any sense. At least in rapture, with the whole Adam thing, it made sense. Why exactly does this guy have powers coming out of his left hand in 1912? Why/how is there a city in the clouds? *spoiler* How the heck did the this whole time continium thing occur!?!? I don't know. To me, it just wasn't Bioshock.

First of all, let me say that I'm strictly an offline player. I don't like going online and playing against strangers. Either I play solo against the AI in tournament or career mode, or my friends and I play co-op against the AI, again in tournament and career mode. So, having a good playing experience against the AI is foremost for me. I'm not going to get into the details of the new defending and tackling. You'll learn how to do that, as you play more and more. The same thing with precision dribbling, etc. I'll just talk about the overall playing experience, in the way that I like to play: against the AI. In that respect, this game is a LOT less fun than Fifa 11. I'm a pretty good player, and in Fifa 11, in World Class difficulty, I can, with some challenges and struggles, win a Premier League season, when playing with a strong team like Manchester United. In 12, it is nearly impossible to win. It all has a very scripted feel, and there are some games that it becomes clear that we will not be allowed to win. When you restart a game at the end of the season (because a loss means you're out of contention) because you lose on a 90 minute goal, and the same thing happens about 3 times, you really question if the outcome is random. We even make a concerted effort, "Let's play really tight defense toward the end of the half and end of the game," and it makes no difference. Stupid things happen to make you lose, such as the AI teammate runs AWAY from the loose ball, in that split second before you take control, so that the opponent takes possession to score. Or, the guy marking the target man on a cross inexplicably moves away to leave him wide open. To give you an illustration of the uselessness of the AI teammates, when I played solo, with ManU, I got beaten by Tottenham 20 times in a row! When playing co-op, where my friend makes intelligent runs, or gets into space, we can usually win or at least tie. None of the attacking strategies from Fifa 11 helps. 1-2 passing does not work, and most of the goal look the same. You pass the ball around, or make angled dribbles, trying to screw up the AI's defensive shape, then make a pass to a striker around the box, who turns and shoots. Crosses are difficult to get in the box, and even when in the box, never seems to get to the striker. Probably headed goals to kicked goals ratio is about 1:20. Finally, EVERY single AI opponent plays like Barcelona. They keep possession with short passes, and if they are ahead with 5 minutes to play, good luck trying to get the ball back. The problem is, you can't play the same style, because the game artificially makes you make an errant pass, after a certain amount of time of possession. When we're ahead, we tried to run out the clock as well, by making doubly sure that the player making the pass was pointed right at the teammate, and making sure the pass was short and safe. But, after about 20 passes, the next one inexplicably goes way off, to the AI opponent. We just look at each other in disbelief... So...I have to say, overall, I'm disappointed. For online play, I've heard it's great, but I'll never know.

GTA3 was a great game and the bar was set pretty high. Vice City, however, has blown it out of the water. First things first-this game is NOT for kids. It contains violence, obscenity, all the adult content of an R-rated movie. No children should be playing this game! Now that we've got that out of the way, it should be noted how great the game is. The great thing about GTA games is their freedom and flexibility. The main focus of the game is on its entertaining missions, during which you make money for yourself, expand your criminal empire, all while punishing the other criminals of Vice City and avoiding police scrutiny. These missions can be started at your discretion. In the meantime, you are always free to walk/drive around the city performing various other functions, such as taxi/pizza delivery/fire/ambulance/police missions, finding ramps off of which to perform unique vehicle stunt jumps, sticking up local stores, or anything else you like. Improvements on this game from GTA3 include --Celebrity voice-overs, including Ray Liotta, Philip Michael Thomas (vastly underrated), Burt Reynolds, Dennis Hopper, and my favorite, Gary Busey. --A police force which is more difficult to elude. --Gangs which are easier to deal with. I hated that after I had finished the GTA3 missions, I couldn't drive around much without being assaulted by gangs which I had previously taken care of. --The ability to buy and control asset properties in order to generate income. --The ability to fly helicopters and planes. No video game is perfect, and there are still some things I would like to see improved. One frustrating aspect it the clunky method of switching between weapons. I can't tell you how many times I tried to switch to my rocket launcher, only to switch to the wrong weapon and pay dearly for it. I also didn't like how the radio stations were too monochromatic and didn't have as much contrast as before. If you don't mind violence, you will love Vice City. It's certainly easy to find now at a great price, and I recommend it

Here we have a side title from Id Software and it is called Rage. Taking a break from the DOOM series it would seem, Id plays with various side concepts here. Right off the bat, there are Final Fantasy 7 references immediately apparent. There are attempts at RPG building, interaction and item use. The game feels like a sci fi version of Desert Solitaire. Nobody does desolation imagery, lonely adventure, thoughtful visuals and suggestive religious iconography like Id Software. Despite this, the game can feel hokey at times, especially in the repetitive buggy driving sequences. It should feel Mad Max yet instead feels very .. middle school afternoon. That or maybe it's there as some kind of Pixar "Cars" tie in. Whatever it is it's slightly annoying, especially given the confined world in which to explore. That said, the limited world available is graphically incredible. Lonely, kind of sad landscapes unfold before the viewer revealing a world that feels vast and desolate. The characters are worn, desperate types who live their unhappy lives trying to survive. Finally strong character interaction comes into play for an Id Software title. More than anything though, this feels like a kind of "preview" for Doom 4. It was Id Software's chance to dabble with genres using their recently made game engine. Time will tell us how much of Rage will carry over into Doom 4. One thing is clearly noticeable, Id is going to need a good melee system. Resident Evil combos or FarCry knife action, something must be done for a melee system over at Id Software.

Binary Domain for the PC is not a disaster of a port, save for the controls. The controls for the game are not very comfortable to play with, if not properly equipped. Even if you have an Xbox 360 controller for windows, the game does not properly map the buttons. Also, the triggers can not be used to map on anything but looking or turning from right to left. Additionally, the sensitivity is too high when trying to aim. The controls are so bad that I cannot even progress through the game at first. To remedy this I had to use a Logitech F series (F310, F510, and F710) gamepads and switch to direct input mode, which it is highly recommended that you buy to safe yourself the trouble. Then all the buttons could be mapped properly, especially the triggers. Binary Domain for the pc may looks amazing for the pc and runs as fast as its console brethren, even on slightly aged pcs. You would do better to definitely purchase this game. It is money well spent. It is not s super long game, but the action is just amazing. You have to experience it for yourself.

When the first Marvel vs Capcom came out, I remember spending at least 500 coins on the arcade machine. When MVC2 came out, I spent some coins, but not as much as I would have liked. MVC2 became a staple of the fighting scene every where in the planet. Come Marvel Vs Capcom 3, maybe the most anticipated fighting game in this generation. Almost everything is retooled except for the chaotic and hectic pace of the game. No longer they are rehashing sprites, now everything is fully modeled in 3D, just as Street Fighter IV and it's super continuation. The control scheme is, in my opinion, the most welcome change. It is simplified enough anyone can pick it up, and complex enough at the same time so skilled players can do insane stuff on the screen. (Low, medium and high attack, partner 1 and 2, and a button labeled: Special, that, alone only does an Air Juggle, with a combination something nice like making Iron-Man fly) The game is made to play with other humans, with friends, or online, it does it's emphasis on playing with other people and not by your own. But for those lone wolves, there is a Mission / Challenge mode, with ten challenges for each character, that serves two purposes: It helps you understand the mechanic of each character, and teaches you the most advanced combo chaining in the game. For completionists, each 5 missions earns you a title. The game is filled with content, that have no doubt, will be expanded through DLC; This is game is too huge and important to let it go to waste and not milk it to death. Capcom understands this perfectly and is making progress into including content At the time of this review, they added something Shadow Battle, a series of fights against the AI of some of the capcom's Staff. I know the pool will continue growing, this game deserves to be played as much if not more, than MVC2. It is that good.

I was excited to pick up my copy of it at my local Gamestop on the day it came out. I had a college class that day, but I first went to Gamestop to pick up my copy. After coming home, I popped it in like it was a big deal. I've had to do updates, which took a while. The gameplay is so fun overall, what sucks about it is the loading times. For instance, when you're about to fight, it takes long for it to start. The scenario campaign mode is like the Tekken Force modes in the previous titles, but this is also the story mode of the game as well. You unlock more characters in the beat em' up portion by simply fighting the characters at the end of each stage, with the help of an A.I. partner, just don't get Alisa near an edge. The online portion has issues with the lag. For those that don't know, it's when you press a button to attack for instance, but the game doesn't react until a second or two later, giving your opponent a chance to beat you down. Despite that, I won most of my matches online. They also did another update of the game by releasing the multiplayer portion of the Scenario Campaign mode, which you play the beat em' up w/another player online and go through rounds of endurance by beating up a lot of baddies. Though the lag exists in that as well. Sometimes, the lag is bad enough that you lose connection to the other player and you go back to the lobby. Your connection depends on where you're playing from and the quality of your internet connection, the better signal that you and the other player you're with, the better. Namco needs to work on the lagging issue.

Fact 1: G1-G5 macro keys do not work wireless. They only function while wired into the computer. A interesting situation considering that G6 - G10 worked wireless. I can't understand the logic Redragon used to limited G1-G5 to only worked wired. Stupidity is a good word to describe Redragon's decision to limit the keyboard's macro keys. Why Redragon? Why???? Why????? Fact 2: F2, F3, & F6-F8 secondary functions are redundant. These keys have dedicated buttons--previous, play/pause, next--and volume knob else where on the keyboard. You can't reprogram them to other functions. Meh. Fact 3: G1-G5 & G6-G10 have different colors when programmed. G1-G5 light up green while G6-G10 light up red when programmed. Meh. Fact 4: Key caps decent for the price. I recommend switching them out for something else because their a bit ugly. Fact 5: This keyboard's software can be easily found on Redragon's site. The side lights can be turned off. A huge plus for those of you who are using this keyboard wireless. Fact 6: The included palm rest does the job. It's not the greatest but it's a palm rest. The magnets are strong. Okay. Fact 7: The volume knob is fast. I don't see lag when using it wired or wireless. Nice job Redragon. Fact 8: Yes, it uses USB-C but the plastic housing surrounding the connector is slimmer than most cables. I have an abundance of Anker & Samsung usb-c cables & none of fit inside the keyboard's port. You might want to find some slim cables. Overall, this keyboard is great for the price. I wish the G1-G5 keys worked wireless because it feels like a waste of space with them not working while wireless. I do suggest you change the key caps because it looks prettier with white key caps. If you really want to make this keyboard better, then you spend money on changing the the body of it. At that point, you'll just better off spending money on other keyboard. I'm going to keep it.

Recently got these on sale for about $400, and at that price you expect quite product. The positives first. They're incredibly light and easy to wear, and look stylish as can be. With just touch sliders for volume and ANC, a direct Xbox Wireless sound connection to the console and no visible microphone arm, I absolutely love the approach to the overall headset. I've had many in my days but never anything as visually and aesthetically pleasing. The sound quality is fantastic overall, but you need to prepared for how they deliver bass: these are not big, beefy "gamer" earcups that have punch and body to the sound. They do deliver bass and they do it well, and they can be EQ'd more to your liking, but with these, I feel like the bass, midrange and treble are like three different points floating in space so to speak, neither one takes over completely. That produces a more balanced, "neutral" sound, but it also means that if you want "body" and bass to every aspect of the sound, you're better off looking at something from SteelSeries (which was my previous set, I'm also looking into the official Xbox Wireless headset soon). Again: fantastic, detailed, immersive soundscape, with pinpoint placement of elements in three dimensions, but if you want that "rock and roll, Hollywood, gamer" sound approach, these are not exactly that. A movie can still rock and rock hard, but not quite in the same way. If most headsets are a clenched fist, this one uses all spread out fingers so to speak. To the downsides though, and a few of them are painfully obvious: with Xbox direct connection you only get 12 hours of battery life, which is a pretty abysmal amount in today's world. After that you have to charge them with USB-C. Charging can take up to three hours depending on your charger unit. Another big one is the sound signal. Yes, when it works the sound is phenomenal, but if you move out of the room you'll experience immediate dropouts. It breaks up, loses connection and turns itself off. I've also had a problem with hissing and crackling, every day, without fail, at some point. Maybe my situation isn't ideal: my Xbox sits behind my TV, and I have wifi signals running to both my phone and the Xbox. I use a wireless controller, and live in an apartment with who knows how many signals in the air. I made sure I was running the Dolby Access app correctly and turned off all sound processing in the B&O app and that helped, but only to a degree. I don't know if it's the actual drivers peaking, signals interfering, or a bit of both, but for $400 dollars you'd expect this to be less of an issue. It's a process, I'm looking into it, and I'll compare these with the official Xbox Wireless headset soon, but be warned, these may not be a clear cut, perfect use flawless diamond every single time. When they do work without issue though, you get a tremendously detailed and immersive and somewhat powerful soundstage that works great for both movies and games. It can be really unforgiving with YouTube and such though: you'll hear every single shortcoming and compressed mic and flaw in the audio. It's a double-edged sword. Be warned. If I could do it over, yes, I would've gone with the cheaper set first just to experiment a little. Are these great? When they work as intended, sure. But are they $400-500 worth of greatness? Not even close.
